newsitem.title: USA: US senators bid to ease plight of legal immigrants.
newsitem.headline: US senators bid to ease plight of legal immigrants.

text.p: Four senior senators Monday said they had launched a bipartisan bid to help ease the plight of many legal immigrants facing a cutoff in federal benefits under a controversial new welfare law.

Sen. Dianne Feinstein, a California Democrat, Sen. John Chafee, a Rhode Island Republican, and two other Republican senators urged Senate Budget Committee Chairman Pete Domenici to allot the highest possible funding to address the matter in the upcoming budget resolution.

"We are writing to ask that as you craft a budget resolution for fiscal year 1998 you consider the plight of these immigrants and provide the highest amount possible within your budgetary constraints for such adjustments," Feinstein, Chafee, and Sens. Alfonse D'Amato of New York and Mike DeWine of Ohio wrote.

The senators said implementation of the new welfare law would cause "considerable upheaval" in the lives of "legal immigrants -- legal residents who work, pay taxes, and contribute enormously to the culture and vitality of our nation."

Advocates for the poor have filed lawsuits in at least two states to block the welfare law, signed by President Clinton in August 1996, charging that denying benefits to legal immigrants was unconstitutional.
Governors have also extended until Aug. 22 an April 1 deadline for states to start culling legal immigrants from the Federal Food Stamps program.
About half the $54.6 billion in six-year savings in the welfare bill comes from denying food stamps and disability aid to legal immigrants.

"For these immigrants -- many of them elderly or disabled -- the approaching deadline represents nothing short of a crisis," the senators wrote in their letter to Domenici, a Republican from New Mexico.
